newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey rejects SAfrican helicopters' sale report.
newsitem.headline: Turkey rejects SAfrican helicopters' sale report.

text.p: Turkish officials on Tuesday rejected reports of a South African government veto on the sale of 12 military helicopters to Turkey on human rights grounds, state-run Anatolian news agency said.

"(The claim) that Turkey's demand to purchase 12 attack helicopters from the South African (arms manufacturer) Denel was blocked by the South African government does not reflect the truth," said defence industry undersecretary Yalcin Burcak.

The South African Sunday Independent said at the weekend a decision to block the 1.2 billion rand ($257 million) sale of the Rooivalk attack helicopters was taken at the last meeting of the National Arms Control Committee on July 17.

Committee chairman Kader Asmal was quoted by the paper as saying the decision had been taken following consideration of Turkey's dominant position in the region, its continuing human rights violations and its illegal occupation of part of Cyprus.

Burcak said the Denel company was more than willing to sell the helicopters to Turkey. He said Turkish authorities refused to buy them since President Nelson Mandela had refused to accept the Ataturk Peace Prize, one of Turkey's highest honours.
South Africa decided on April 15 to lift an arms embargo it had imposed on Turkey in April 1995 after a Turkish incursion into northern Iraq against separatist Kurdish guerrillas.
Turkey imposed a tit-for-tat embargo on arms sales to South Africa after the 1995 ban, but indicated that its lifting was a formality following South Africa's decision this April.
